title: Tagged run satisfies recorded-run conditions
statement: Let $R$ be a machine whose states are tagged phase states, and let $M$ be a machine with phase states indexed by $i$. Suppose that through every time $u\le t$, the run of $R$ from $a$ agrees with the run of $M$ from $c$ after tagging its state by $i$. Suppose the run of $R$ from $a$ reaches $b$ after $t+1$ steps, the phase index $i$ differs from the phase indices of both distinguished states $\mathrm{yes}$ and $\mathrm{no}$, and the work-head distances from the specified base positions are at most $r$ at every time $u\le t$ in the run of $M$ and at time $t+1$ in configuration $b$. Then the run of $R$ from $a$ to $b$ in $t+1$ steps avoids both distinguished states at all earlier times and has all work-head distances from the base positions at most $r$ at every time through $t+1$.
hypotheses_covered: A natural number $K$, symbol type $\Gamma$, phase index type $I$, and phase state types $\mathrm{Ph}(i)$
A base position for each of the $K$ tapes and radius $r\in\mathbb{N}$
Configurations $a,b$ for $R$ and phase machine $M$ with index $i$ and configuration $c$
For every $u\le t$, $R$'s run from $a$ agrees with the run of $M$ from $c$ after tagging by $i$
$i$ differs from the phase index of $\mathrm{yes}$
$i$ differs from the phase index of $\mathrm{no}$
At every $u\le t$ and on every tape, the run of $M$ has head distance from the base at most $r$
In $b$, every work-head distance from the base is at most $r$
